highlights: Google, the most vertically integrated of them all, with its TPU chips and its Gemini models. As I wrote on Tuesday in ‘Google Specializes Its TPUs as Nvidia Wobbles’ (AI-RTZ #1266), its TPU teams get early access to the latest Gemini models to design and debug the chips.

Amazon, with its Trainium chips and its own Nova models. Anthropic is one of Trainium’s biggest customers, as I discussed in ‘Amazon AI chips traction with key customers & partners’ (AI-RTZ #1094). [...] Now that same Anthropic is using Claude to design chips of its own. Every custom chip of Anthropic’s that works could mean fewer Trainium chips rented from Amazon, or fewer TPUs from Google, over time. Its biggest backers are also its chip suppliers, and soon perhaps its chip competitors.

If Anthropic or OpenAI end up with AI models far better at chip design than anyone else’s, they could keep the most cutting-edge versions to themselves, at least at first. [...] OpenAI is already there with its ‘Jalapeño’ chip, designed with help from its own frontier AI models. Meanwhile, the companies building the backup chips to Nvidia, Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta, are all building their own AI models. The frontier AI labs are crossing over into chips, and the chipmakers into models.
